IAP Shishu Bhavan · Majjigenahalli, Shivamogga

A rural centre for child health and free learning

IAP Shivamogga is building Shishu Bhavan as a child health facility. The branch proposes an education centre on the same campus to create and host free, self-paced courses for underserved schools and colleges across the district.

The case for partnership

Child health closer to home. Learning that travels.

Shishu Bhavan gives IAP Shivamogga a physical base for child health services and a way to share free learning beyond the campus. The two packages address different barriers and can be measured separately.

01 / Child health

Bring developmental support closer

Plan local paediatric consultations, developmental screening and referral support. Record where families currently go for follow-up and what gets in the way.

02 / Education

Make useful lessons free to revisit

Start with health literacy and digital and AI literacy. Offer self-paced modules in English with Kannada as a second language, plus activities teachers can use in class.

03 / Access

Plan for shared devices and weak connections

Test text, lightweight downloads and offline access with schools before buying equipment for a wider rollout.

Shivamogga taluk · First outreach

The IAP team has approached government primary and high schools in Durgigudi. Participation is pending. The first school conversations can help establish device access, connectivity, language preferences and the topics teachers want most.

Six more taluks · Potential expansion

Bhadravathi, Hosanagara, Sagara, Shikaripura, Soraba and Thirthahalli are potential expansion areas. The team can prioritise institutions using pilot results, local demand and delivery readiness. Shivamogga district’s official taluk list.

01 / The learning experience

Try a lesson the way a learner would

The proposed catalogue starts with health literacy and digital and AI literacy. English is the primary teaching language, with Kannada as a second language. Short lessons, practice and instant feedback let learners work independently, while educator guides and lightweight downloads support classroom use.

Illustrative module · Digital literacy

02 / Proposed delivery

Start with a pilot, then expand

The team has approached government primary and high schools in Durgigudi. Participation is pending confirmation. The pilot would start by choosing age-appropriate topics with teachers and testing how students access the lessons. College outreach is part of the district-wide plan.

01

Build with educators

Choose topics with pilot institutions, write lessons and review them before release.

02

Host locally and test access

Serve courses from IAP-managed servers. Test downloads and shared-device use in partner institutions. Size GPUs against measured workloads such as transcription or approved-content tutoring.

03

Measure who learns

Report unique learners, module completion, pre/post learning checks and repeat use by educators. Use the results to guide expansion.

03 / Partnership

Two ways to fund one project

A lead CSR partner can support both packages under one agreement, or partners can fund either package separately. Each package has its own deliverables, budget and milestones.

Package A / Facility

Complete and equip Shishu Bhavan

Fund verified remaining works and initial fit-out. Release grants against agreed construction and commissioning milestones.

Package B / Education

Launch the free learning programme

Fund course production, Kannada adaptation, educator onboarding, local hosting and evaluation. Size GPU purchases once workloads, supplier quotations and running costs are reviewed.

Lead partnership

Support the campus and the pilot

Agree one plan with separate budgets and reporting for building works and learning outcomes.

Planning figures for discussion. The original facility estimate was ₹3.5–4 crore for construction and initial setup. The draft education model was ₹1.60 crore over 24 months. The team will confirm the cost of remaining works, the first pilot budget and any shared costs before setting the grant amount.

06 / Funder questions

What a partner can review before committing

How would grant spending be tracked?

The proposed grant structure uses separate budgets for the facility and education packages, milestone-linked disbursements, and expenditure and utilisation reporting. The facility package can use engineer-certified progress. The education package can report modules delivered, participation and learning outcomes.

How will the centre cover recurring costs?

The operating budget needs to cover staffing, electricity, connectivity, backups, maintenance and equipment replacement. Partners can review the annual costs and funding plan before a multi-year commitment. Course access is proposed to remain free.

What would justify buying GPUs?

Start with measured workloads such as transcription or tutoring from approved course material. Compare the cost of local hardware over its useful life with hosted options. Test downloadable lessons and shared-device use with pilot schools before funding wider deployment.

How would the programme protect children and student data?

Agree content review and safeguarding procedures with pilot institutions. Define which learner data is needed, who can access it and how long it is retained. Give funders aggregate reporting and test any AI tutoring with educator oversight before wider release.
